definitions.explanation: The supreme military commander who held de facto political power in Japan, particularly during the Kamakura, Muromachi, and Edo periods. Short for {征夷大将軍|せいいたいしょうぐん}.
A high-ranking military officer. Used in historical and modern military contexts.

examples.japanese: {徳川|とくがわ}{家康|いえやす}は{初代|しょだい}{将軍|しょうぐん}だ。
examples.english: Tokugawa Ieyasu was the first shogun.

examples.japanese: {将軍|しょうぐん}は{江戸城|えどじょう}に{住|す}んでいた。
examples.english: The shogun lived in Edo Castle.

examples.japanese: {鎌倉|かまくら}{幕府|ばくふ}は{源|みなもとの}{頼朝|よりとも}が{将軍|しょうぐん}に{任命|にんめい}されて{成立|せいりつ}した。
examples.english: The Kamakura shogunate was established when Minamoto no Yoritomo was appointed shogun.

examples.japanese: {将軍|しょうぐん}が{軍|ぐん}を{指揮|しき}する。
{彼|かれ}は{若|わか}くして{将軍|しょうぐん}に{昇進|しょうしん}した。
examples.english: He was promoted to general at a young age.

examples.japanese: {戦場|せんじょう}で{将軍|しょうぐん}が{自|みずか}ら{先頭|せんとう}に{立|た}って{兵|へい}を{率|ひき}いた。
examples.english: On the battlefield, the general personally led the troops from the front.

notes:
CULTURAL CONTEXT:
The full title is {征夷大将軍|せいいたいしょうぐん} (commander-in-chief of the expeditionary force against the barbarians), abbreviated to {将軍|しょうぐん}. The {将軍|しょうぐん} was the effective ruler of Japan during the feudal period, while the {天皇|てんのう} (emperor) retained symbolic authority. The three major shogunates were:
- {鎌倉|かまくら}{幕府|ばくふ} (1185–1333)
- {室町|むろまち}{幕府|ばくふ} (1336–1573)
- {江戸|えど}{幕府|ばくふ} (1603–1868)

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {征夷大将軍|せいいたいしょうぐん}: shogun (full title)
- {将軍|しょうぐん}{家|け}: the shogun's household/family
- {将軍|しょうぐん}に{任命|にんめい}される: to be appointed shogun
